PSG also claim they have “identified a solution for replacing the pitch at the Parc des Princes for the upcoming matches,” starting with its next home game in Ligue 1 against Monaco on 4 September.

Sports.title: ‘He must resign’: Fans’ petition calls for Infantino to quit as Fifa president
Sports.content:
Fans’ groups worldwide have launched a petition calling for the resignation of Gianni Infantino as Fifa president and for wholesale reform of the organisation.

Infantino is under mounting pressure after being forced to abandon plans to seek private investment to run Fifa tournaments, including the men’s and women’s World Cups.

Three continental confederations accused Infantino of “deception” in an open letter last week over the manner the plan was devised and presented, with Uefa, European football’s governing body, intent on boycotting Fifa events having “lost confidence” in Infantino’s leadership.

Infantino retains support, notably in Africa and South America, but now fans’ organisations have called on him to step down, with a petition being launched on change.org.

“The shameful attempt by one individual – the Fifa president himself – to sell off the World Cup to private investors exposed a betrayal football will never forget,” a statement on behalf of the fan organisations said. “Infantino’s plan was stitched together in secret. Negotiated behind closed doors. Hidden from Fifa’s own members and from the millions of people whose passion makes football what it is.”

Fans are being encouraged to sign the petition, which already has support from all six Fifa confederations spanning continental and national fan groups. “A president who repeatedly betrays football and makes a mockery of our game has lost the right to lead it,” the statement continued. “For the credibility of Fifa – and for the future of the game – he must resign.”

The petition also calls for reform of Fifa, including the formal involvement of supporters and other key football stakeholders in decisions that shape the future of the game.

“The departure of Gianni Infantino is a first and a must, but that can only have a positive impact if it’s followed by some reform of the office and of governance,” said Ronan Evain, the executive director of Football Supporters Europe, which is a signatory to the petition. “If a man can concentrate so many powers then the governance of Fifa is not fit for purpose.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“[Fifa] needs to start from scratch. All the reforms from 2016 have been erased or made irrelevant by Infantino. We need to be as open-minded as possible on the future of football governance and there are other models outside football, outside sport, that need to be looked into – the idea of rotating presidencies seems interesting.”

Fifa has been approached for comment.

Sports.title: Opening half-hour of TNT Sports’ Premier League broadcasts to be shown on YouTube
Sports.content:
TNT Sports will make the first 30 minutes of their live Premier League broadcasts available on YouTube this season starting with Manchester United’s visit to Hull on Saturday.

The pre-Premier League show EKO – Early Kick Off – will be available free-to-air for the first time, as well as on TNT Sports and the streaming service HBO Max.

Presented by Liam MacDevitt or Olivia Buzaglo, EKO will start at 11am and feature the early team news from the game, which is released 75 minutes before kick-off, and the pre-match thoughts of TNT’s main pundits such as Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole. The Saturday lunchtime live games kick off at 12.30pm live on TNT and HBO Max.

In another departure for TNT, EKO will be broadcast before all of their live Premier League games this season rather than just before their Saturday lunchtime kick-offs, as was the case last season. As a result, TNT’s coverage of an 8pm Saturday kick-off will begin with an EKO programme starting at 6.30pm.

The 30-minute show will have a magazine-type tone and feature discussion of wider issues rather than just the game itself, such as transfers and new players, in an attempt to broaden TNT’s match audience.

“TNT’s coverage is evolving and this will help us reach more football fans earlier in the day,” Scott Young, an executive vice-president at the parent company, Warner Bros Discovery Europe, said.

“We have a large number of loyal subscribers, but it’s also important to reach fans off-platform. I think everyone is really looking forward to the return of the Premier League, especially after the excitement generated by the World Cup.”

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Newcastle to sign Manchester City’s Nico González?
Sports.content:
A Manchester City clearout is in the offing, which could aid Newcastle’s search for a new central midfielder to replace the departed Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães. Nico González could be packing his bags to head up to St James’ Park, having never quite proven himself at the Etihad Stadium. Attacking players Omar Marmoush and Savinho, meanwhile, are on their way to Tottenham, which should kickstart a busy end to the window at City.

On the other side of Manchester, United are looking to sell off some of their younger players to Arsenal. The Gibraltar international James Scanlon, who spent the second half of last season on loan at Swindon, and Habeeb Ogunneye are set for moves to the Premier League champions. The Gunners are ramping up their recruitment of young players to strengthen quality across the club. On his way out of the Emirates Stadium is another youngster, with Ethan Nwaneri wanted by Fulham and Everton, while RB Leipzig could also come into the mix for a loan move. Gabriel Jesus has also been linked with an exit but the Brazilian wants to stick around at the Emirates.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ezri Konsa is on his way to Arsenal, so Unai Emery needs a replacement. One man on the radar is the Chelsea defender Tosin Adarabioyo, who is surplus to requirements, but Marseille may compete for his signature. It is hard to keep up with Aston Villa’s antics at the moment, so Ajax engaging them in talks over a potential move for Leon Bailey may have been missed by the less discerning rumour mongers. The Jamaica international has a year remaining on his deal at Villa Park.

It may not seem like Everton are getting much done, but they are supposedly working on things in the background. In addition to Nwaneri, Como’s Assane Diao is a winger attracting their attention and a bid could be made for the Ivorian – but with a potential £60m price tag, whether it comes to anything is unlikely.

Hectic Hull, as they may soon be known amid their plotting in the transfer market, are set to miss out Niccolo Fortini after his club, Fiorentina, agreed a deal with Torino. The blow may be softened if they can get a deal over the line for Nottingham Forest’s Dilane Bakwa. Crystal Palace cannot afford to sell any of their key players but Galatasaray have called up with an offer for Ismaïla Sarr, which was quickly rejected.

Championship side Wrexham are trying to ramp up their summer transfer business with a move for Plymouth’s Bim Pepple but could face competition from Preston for the striker, while a host of clubs in Europe and MLS are also monitoring the former Luton man. Another player Wrexham may move for is Leeds forward Lukas Nmecha, although that seems a tad optimistic.

Sports.title: Six midfielders Man City have considered this summer to replace Rodri – with two signings expected
Sports.content:
Six midfielders Man City have considered this summer to replace Rodri – with two signings expected

Manchester City are expected to sign two more midfielders before the window slams shut, talkSPORT understands.

The Citizens are on the lookout for reinforcements having sold Rodri and Tijjani Reijnders earlier this week to Barcelona and Al Qadsiah respectively.

5 City boss Maresca is desperate for reinforcements in midfield Credit: Getty

It has been a summer of change at the Etihad, with Enzo Maresca replacing Pep Guardiola in the dugout.

Along with selling Rodri and Reijnders, City have also parted ways with fellow midfielder Bernardo Silva.

While John Stones, Nathan Ake, James Trafford and Manuel Akanji have all moved on.

City have made just the one major midfield signing this summer - bringing in Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest in a £116million club-record transfer.

What midfielders are on Man City's radar?

It is believed that City have identified six potential options to bolster their side in the middle of the pitch.

We told you on Wednesday how the club are prepared to bid for Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea's deadline passing.

The Blues set a 5pm deadline for last Friday for any potential suitors to stump up an offer for the £120m-rated World Cup winner.

And it has been said that Fernandez would be open to a reunion with ex-Blues boss Maresca.

Meanwhile, City remain in advanced to talks with Lille over the signing of teenage starlet Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Personal terms have already been in place for the 18-year-old since July.

5 Fernandez could swap Stamford Bridge for the Etihad before the window closes Credit: Getty

5 Bouaddi is regarded as one of the world's most talented youngsters Credit: Getty

As talkSPORT reported at the beginning of July, Lille are seeking a fee of €100m (£85.7m) for the Morocco international.

They are willing to discount the price if a loan or pre-agreement can be reached with City, although the English club's preference is to sign and keep him.

Elsewhere, as talkSPORT revealed last week, interest remains in Adam Wharton having made an enquiry for the Crystal Palace star.

City have been told by Rangers legend and talkSPORT co-host Ally McCoist they should prioritise a move to sign the 22-year-old.

Fernandez's Argentina teammate Alexis Mac Allister is also appreciated, while Liverpool have no plans to sell the former Brighton maestro this window.

Meanwhile, Bournemouth's Alex Scott is admired by City, as talkSPORT first reported in July.

5 Wharton has won three trophies - including the Conference League last season - since joining Palace in February 2024 Credit: Getty

5 Mac Allister is unlikely to be sold by Liverpool this summer, despite being admired by City Credit: Getty

City made an approach to sign Scott last month, though the Cherries insist the 22-year-old is not for sale.

The south coast side have already rejected a £64m offer from Chelsea this summer.

And lastly, Roma's Manu Kone is under consideration by City following an impressive World Cup for France.

The 25-year-old had been on Manchester United's list of targets, and was also linked with a move to Arsenal.

Sports.title: Will there be hydration breaks in the Premier League this season?
Sports.content:
Will there be hydration breaks in the Premier League this season?

The Premier League returns for the start of the 2026/27 season this weekend following a summer filled with hydration breaks.

All 20 clubs are in action across Friday to Monday as a new campaign of top-flight football gets underway.



3 Hydration breaks were a controversial aspect of this summer's World Cup Credit: AFP

As well as a raft of new signings and three promoted clubs, a string of rule changes have been introduced.

Those include new areas for VAR to intervene, substitution changes and time-wasting deterrents.

Several of those features have previously been seen during the World Cup earlier this summer.



Another fixture of the tournament was the controversial hydration breaks.

Despite the negative response from supporters in North America and watching at home, the stoppages continued until the end of the World Cup.



However, will they be used in the Premier League this season?

What are hydration breaks in football?

FIFA's controversial hydration breaks were introduced for the 2026 World Cup in Canada, Mexico and the USA.

Following concerns over soaring temperatures at last year's Club World Cup, they were implemented as a counter-measure to aid players during matches.



The mandatory three-minute stoppages occurred once in each half around the midway point.

3 Mandatory three-minute stoppages were used during matches at the World Cup Credit: Getty

Once signalled by the referee, players would be able to take on liquids on the touchline whilst also receiving instructions from coaching staff.

Meanwhile, live TV broadcasts were permitted to show adverts during the hydration breaks.



As the World Cup progressed, the negative response to the stoppages extended to fans booing them from inside the stadium during matches.

FIFA's head of global football development Arsene Wenger revealed after the tournament that the use of hydration breaks would be reviewed.

Their change in stance was influenced by the reaction from supporters to the stoppages in play.

Premier League 26/27 opening fixtures 3pm kick-offs unless stated Friday, August 22 Arsenal vs Coventry - 8pm, live on talkSPORT Saturday, August 23 Hull vs Manchester United - 12.30pm, live on talkSPORT

Everton vs Crystal Palace

Ipswich vs Sunderland

Nottingham Forest vs Leeds

Brentford vs Tottenham - 5.30pm Sunday, August 24 Brighton vs Aston Villa - 2pm

Manchester City vs Bournemouth - 2pm

Newcastle vs Liverpool - 4.30pm Monday, August 25 Fulham vs Chelsea - 8pm, live on talkSPORT

Will the Premier League use hydration breaks this season?

Hydration breaks will not be implemented by the Premier League during the 2026/27 season.



Instead, matches will continue through to half-time and full-time in each half without planned stoppages.

It comes despite hydration breaks featuring in the Carabao Cup and EFL already this season.

Those stoppages have been met with loud jeers from supporters inside the stadiums at matches featuring the breaks.

Referees had signalled for hydration breaks at selected matches amid the recent UK heatwave.



The Premier League has previously implemented water breaks in the past, though.

3 Hydration breaks will not be used in the Premier League this season Credit: Getty

They were first introduced during Project Restart in 2020 after the 2019/20 season resumed in June before running into July.

Matches had been suspended in March of the same year due to the Covid-19 pandemic.



Water breaks were later reintroduced at the start of the 2022/23 season.

The move came after amber weather warnings were enforced due to extreme heat in areas of England and Wales ahead of the opening weekend.

Sports.title: Top ten most expensive summer transfers so far: Chelsea, Man City and Spurs all confirm £100m deals
Sports.content:
Top ten most expensive summer transfers so far: Chelsea, Man City and Spurs all confirm £100m deals

Premier League clubs have been hard at work splashing the cash this summer, with three clubs already completing nine-figure deals.

The transfer record for a British player has been broken with Chelsea sealing the £117million capture of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.



11 Rogers has joined Chelsea in a blockbuster deal

The 2026 summer window officially opened on June 15, with talkSPORT.com already providing a completed list of every deal.

Due to certain PSR constraints, some initial-loan agreements in previous windows have since become permanent this summer.

The rising inflation in the transfer market also means relegation is no longer a signal for clubs to poach key players on the cheap.



With that in mind, teams have had to open up their chequebooks. Below are the top 10 most expensive arrivals in the Premier League...

10. Andrey Santos (Chelsea to Manchester United) – £50m

talkSPORT understands the Red Devils paid £48m plus £2m in achievable add-ons to land the Brazilian midfielder from the Blues.



Newcastle were also understood to be keen on Chelsea's former No.17, who has now taken the same shirt number at Old Trafford.

The 22-year-old only made 13 Premier League starts last season, nearly half of which came under his ex-Strasbourg manager Liam Rosenior, during the latter's four-month tenure as Chelsea boss.



United prioritised central midfield reinforcements this summer following Casemiro's exit, with Manuel Ugarte also rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament at the World Cup.

11 Man United's new signing Andrey Santos made his unofficial debut against Wrexham in Helsinki Credit: Getty

9. Maxence Lacroix (Crystal Palace to Chelsea) - £52m

Chelsea have spent upwards of £330m this summer, including announcing Maxence Lacroix has joined the club.

The French centre-back signed for £52m, matching Jan Paul van Hecke's move from Brighton to Tottenham.



After joining, Lacroix labelled the club as the 'best in the world' and said he matched the desire of manager Alonso.

He has also become the 14th most expensive defender ever in the Premier League following his big-money move.

11 Lacroix has left Crystal Palace to sign for Chelsea in a big-money deal Credit: Getty

8. Jan Paul van Hecke (Brighton to Tottenham) – £52m

The Netherlands defender's move to Spurs wasn't part of the deal that saw Vuskovic head in the opposite direction.



However, on the balance sheet, Roberto De Zerbi reunited with his former Brighton player for a nominal fee, all things considered.

Tottenham were persistent in their bid to land Van Hecke, with Seagulls CEO Paul Barber revealing on talkSPORT that the Lilywhites had two previous bids rejected.

The Dutchman, who cost Brighton just £1.8m from NAC Breda in 2020, was entering the final year of his contract with Hurzeler's side.

11 De Zerbi has worked with the Dutch defender before on the south coast Credit: AFP



7. Johan Manzambi (Freiburg to Aston Villa) - £52m

Unai Emery's side have been involved in the biggest transfer of the summer so far, but have also broken their club record on a player.

The West Midlands club snapped up Manzambi for £52m, which surpassed the £50m forked out to land Amadou Onana in 2024.

Newcastle were close to signing the midfielder, having agreed a deal in principle with Freiburg for £51m, before Villa swooped in.

The 20-year-old played against Villa in the Europa League final, while he also scored three goals for Switzerland in the World Cup but is struggling with a knee injury ahead of the new season.



11 Villa broke their transfer record to sign the Switzerland midfielder Credit: Getty Images

6. Jeremy Jacquet (Rennes to Liverpool) – £60m

Liverpool completed the biggest deal of the winter window's deadline day by beating Chelsea to land the France U21 international.

talkSPORT understands that the Reds agreed an initial £55m to sign Jacquet, with a further £5m to be paid in potential add-ons.

A move for the defender eclipsed the £52m fee spent by Manchester City on Jeremy Doku in 2023 to become Rennes' record sale.



However, the 21-year-old spent the second half of last season at his boyhood club, with a move to Anfield only becoming official on July 1.

11 Guimaraes is now an Arsenal star Credit: Getty

5. Bruno Guimaraes (Newcastle to Arsenal) – £75m

Amid the swathe of departures at Newcastle, former Toon captain Guimaraes as headed to the champions.

The Brazil star has signed a four-year deal in north London and called the move one of the 'toughest decisions' of his life.



The 28-year-old scored 31 goals in 195 appearances for Newcastle, having joined them from Lyon for £40m in 2022.

"I'm at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this," Guimaraes said. "I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I'm in the right place to do it. I'm so excited to start."

11 Jacquet inherited Ibrahima Konate's No.5 shirt at Liverpool Credit: Getty

4. Mateus Fernandes (West Ham to Tottenham) – £85m

Spurs have broken their transfer record twice this summer, the first of which saw Fernandes arrive from their relegated London rivals.



The 22-year-old was one of the standout Premier League midfielders last season, despite West Ham's struggles.

He scored five top-flight goals and registered four assists in 41 appearances but missed out on Portugal's World Cup squad.

However, Troy Deeney told talkSPORT that he questioned whether Fernandes was really the player to 'change the mentality' at Tottenham after his successive relegations, having also failed to beat the drop at Southampton.

11 Spurs beat off competition from Manchester United to secure Fernandes' signature Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



3. Sandro Tonali (Newcastle to Tottenham) – £100m

Spurs shattered their transfer record again to poach the Italian from Newcastle less than a week after unveiling Fernandes.

Tonali joined De Zerbi's side in a £100m deal - an initial £92.5m fee with £7.5m in proposed add-ons.

The 26-year-old made 110 appearances across his three seasons with Newcastle after his reported £52m move from AC Milan in July 2023.

But he was accused by talkSPORT Breakfast co-host Gabriel Agbonlahor of joining Tottenham 'for the big bucks'.



11 Tonali is the latest key player to leave St. James' Park after signing for Tottenham Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

2. Elliot Anderson (Nottingham Forest to Manchester City) – £116m

Man City were the first of two clubs to break the transfer record for a British player following their capture of Anderson at the start of July.

The England international sealed his move to the Etihad Stadium from Nottingham Forest for a fixed £116m fee while at the World Cup.

Forest have tried to claim the deal is worth a total of £130m, which would eclipse the Premier League transfer record set by Liverpool's £125m signing of Alexander Isak, but City dispute this.



Anderson featured in all of England's games during their run to third at the World Cup - their best finish at the tournament since 1966.

11 Anderson put in some heroic midfield performances Credit: talKSPORT

1. Morgan Rogers (Aston Villa to Chelsea) - £117m

Anderson's reign as the most expensive British player lasted mere weeks as his England teammate Rogers took the crown.

The 23-year-old was the leading target at Arsenal, but he has now signed a six-year deal, with the option of another 12 months, at their London rivals Chelsea.



"I'm so excited," Rogers said on the move.

"For me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I've always admired since I was a kid.

11 Rogers made three starts and a further four sub appearances for England at the World Cup Credit: Getty

"I'm really excited about the project with the new manager, the players we've got and where the club is heading. That's why I'm here, and I can't wait to get started.

"The way the club wants to go and how it wants to move forward, it's something I want to be a part of, and I think it was just perfect for me.



"I'm a free spirit, free-flowing footballer. I like to take risks, make things happen, change games. Whatever that may take. Just can't wait to get started."

Head over to talkSPORT BET for all the latest transfer odds ahead of the key moves this summer

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford sent clear message after biting back at Gary Neville
Sports.content:
Alan Brazil has told Marcus Rashford to focus on his football after the Manchester United star hit out at Gary Neville.

Rashford, who is back in the Man United fold following successive loan spells at Aston Villa and Barcelona, took issue with United legend Neville trying to bring him up on The Overlap.



3 Rashford wasn't happy with Neville's comments Credit: Getty

Carragher sticks up for Rashford

"Marcus Rashford, what do we think? Last question," Neville posed in a clip of an upcoming episode of the podcast, much to the annoyance of co-host Jamie Carragher.

"Oh f****** hell!," the Liverpool great reacted. "Can we do a podcast without mentioning Rashford? Stop it! Oh my god".

Rashford later thanked Carragher for his support, posting on X: "Thanks, Jamie.



"It would be great to be able to get my head down and play football without my name being mentioned every day" – followed by a crying emoji.

But Brazil found it odd Rashford expected to be able to stay out of the limelight given his high profile.



"Marcus Rashford says he wants to play football with his name being mentioned every day," Brazil noted on Thursday's talkSPORT Breakfast with Gabby Agbonlahor. "Strange thing to say, isn't it, Gab?"

Agbonlahor, who made over 300 Premier League appearances for Aston Villa, urged Rashford: "Just ignore it".



Encouraging Rashford to work on getting back to his best, Ipswich Town icon Brazil – who later played for Man United himself – said: "You enjoyed last year, Marcus, at the brilliant Barcelona. You're now back at United. Listen, one stage you were brilliant there. Just concentrate and get back to that. I don't care what people say."

Sharing his co-host's view, Agbonlahor continued: "You've got to switch off from what anyone says about you in the media as a player, Alan.

Rashford 'has to focus constantly'

"You've got to ignore it and just go and play your football. Why are you looking at these podcasts?"

3 Rashford helped England finish third at this summer's World Cup, their best performance since 1966 Credit: Getty



"That's the problem with social media," Brazil added. "He's got to just focus constantly [on his football]."

Rashford hasn't made a competitive appearance for Man United since December 2024, falling out of favour with then boss Ruben Amorim.

But Michael Carrick has reintegrated the 28-year-old England forward into the squad at his boyhood club.

Rashford played his first game for United in the best part of two years when he came off the bench in last Saturday's final pre-season friendly against AC Milan.



Rashford 'in great spirits'

And while Rashford's future at Old Trafford is still uncertain, Carrick is pleased to have him at his disposal, saying recently: "He's our player and he's come back great. He's just like any other player.

"I've known Marcus a long time and he gives us something a little bit different. And he's been in great spirits since he's been back.

3 Rashford played 29 minutes for United against Milan at the weekend Credit: Getty

"He's been back two or three days training and it's just pretty normal, to be honest. And we're looking forward to the start of the season."



Rashford could potentially be involved as Man United kick off the 2026/27 Premier League campaign away to newly promoted Hull City on Saturday, live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Simon Jordan blasts ‘grotesquely unfair’ transfer rules with Arsenal and Man United to blame
Sports.content:
Simon Jordan believes the Premier League's transfer rules are 'grotesquely unfair' amid Aston Villa's dismantling this summer.

Villa, along with Newcastle, have sold many of their key players that helped them challenge the 'Big Six' in recent years.

3 Aston Villa's Europa League-winning squad has been pulled apart this summer Credit: Getty

Unai Emery's side won the Europa League just a few months ago, but they've now lost Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, with Ezri Konsa on the brink of joining Arsenal.

Rogers joined Chelsea for a record £117m, while Tielemans signed for Manchester United and Digne was sold to PSG.

As for Newcastle, who were playing in the Champions League last season, they have seen multiple stars depart this summer.

Bruno Guimaraes will be joined by Konsa at Arsenal, with Anthony Gordon going to Barcelona and Sandro Tonali to Tottenham.

The two clubs have now been significantly weakened heading into the new Premier League season due to their sales.

Meanwhile, Chelsea and Spurs, who hugely struggled last term, have been spending huge amounts of money in recent weeks.

And talkSPORT host Jordan is not happy with how the transfer window has panned out, slamming the financial rules.

He believes the rules have helped protect the 'Big Six' from being challenged at the top of the Premier League.

Jordan slams 'unfair' transfer rules

Speaking on Aston Villa and Newcastle's tough summers, Jordan said: "I felt that Newcastle weren't going to be in a position to challenge the legacy clubs because they're not being allowed to.

"It's grotesquely unfair that the Liverpools, the Arsenals, the Manchester Uniteds, Man Citys, the Spurs can spend as much money as they wish.

3 Spurs took one of Newcastle's stars for £100m despite almost being relegated last season Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Why can the big clubs keep spending so much? Manchester United, Manchester City, Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool and Tottenham are all benefiting from the squad-cost ratio rules. The new SCR rules in the Premier League allow teams to spend 85% of their total revenue on player costs. Therefore, the clubs with higher revenues, such as the Big Six, will have more money available to spend on transfers. Those playing in Europe have a lower cap of 70%, but that amount of money would still be higher for bigger clubs than 85% at smaller clubs. Exceeding the caps significantly will lead to fines and other punishments, so clubs must follow them strictly.

"No one else can because they can generate the turnover because they're now seeded. So Aston Villa and Newcastle can get on with it.

"They can't do what Chelsea did. They can't do what Man City did.

"That was break up the orthodoxy of Arsenal and Manchester United and because they can't buy their way into the positions that Man City and Chelsea were able to do.

"You can't build a team to challenge in perpetuity and be a top side.

"It is absolutely the fault of the Man Uniteds and Arsenals because they dressed up the idea of financial fair play as some governance to retain the sanity of the game and it's nothing of the sort.

"It's unfair. It's pulling up the drawbridge and saying to everybody else 'We're in the room now and you can't join'."

3 Chelsea broke a British transfer record to sign Rogers from Aston Villa Credit: AFP

The Premier League is a 'closed shop'

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters believes that every team should aspire to win the top-flight title.

But that's something that Coventry City owner Doug King thinks isn't realistic due to the current financial rules - and similarly to Jordan, he struggles to see a way in which a smaller team can challenge.

When asked for his verdict on Masters' view, King said on talkSPORT's White and Jordan: "You can aspire, but...it's a closed shop.

"It's a squad cost ratio, you've got £800m revenues versus £200m revenues, you can do the maths.

"It's going to be incredibly difficult, so you have to find every advantage you can to be competitive.

"Our goal is to try and build momentum. We need to be in a position to stay in the league if we can, and then build those revenues towards.

"We're never going to get towards those numbers, but build them towards some meaningful revenues so we can be competitive."

Sports.title: How many Premier League managerial changes have there been this summer?
Sports.content:
How many Premier League managerial changes have there been this summer?

The Premier League has had a managerial shake-up for next season, with ten clubs making changes in the dugout.

With the new campaign nearly upon us, half the division will have managers competing in the Premier League for the first time with their respective clubs.

10 Pep Guardiola bid farewell to Manchester City in May after a decade at the club Credit: Getty

Pep Guardiola decided to leave Manchester City at the end of last season after winning 20 major trophies with the side.

The longest-serving manager is now Mikel Arteta, who has served as the Arsenal boss for over six years, and will be the only Premier League-winning manager on the touchline.

Chelsea and Manchester United made big decisions at the end of last season and have spent the summer rebuilding with their new head coaches at the helm.

However, some clubs like Newcastle have lost their manager amid pre-season preparations and have precious time to prepare ahead of the new campaign.

Manchester City - Enzo Maresca replaces Pep Guardiola

Guardiola's ten-year reign at City ended ahead of the final day of the 2024/25 season.

Enzo Maresca eventually replaced the Spaniard, having previously spent time at the club as a youth coach.

The Italian manager left Chelsea in hostile circumstances in January following the Blues' FIFA Club World Cup win, despite having three-and-a-half years left on his contract.

His coaching style has been heavily influenced by Guardiola, and he will want to guide the club through a turbulent transition following the departures of experienced squad members like John Stones, Nathan Ake, and Bernardo Silva.

The 46-year-old has shown he can win trophies despite his relatively short career, having previously guided the Leicester City to the Championship title.

10 Man United have been on an upwards trajectory since Michael Carrick's interim appointment in January Credit: Getty

Manchester United - Michael Carrick (made permanent)

After the sacking of Ruben Amorim, Michael Carrick was put in charge of the side on an interim basis.

The 45-year-old made it impossible for the Old Trafford hierarchy not to sign him permanently after securing Champions League football for next season.

Since taking charge in January, Carrick won more points per game (2.29) than any other Premier League manager.

His first full-time managerial role was spent at Middlesborough, where he reached the 2022/23 playoffs and the EFL Cup semi-finals the following year.

He signed a two-year contract to remain as boss in May, with United's win at Brighton marking his first official game as permanent manager.

10 New Liverpool boss Iraola is looking to re-shape the club's attack Credit: AFP

Liverpool - Andoni Iraola replaces Arne Slot

Arne Slot was expected to continue as Liverpool head coach after eventually securing Champions League qualification for next season.

However, the Liverpool hierarchy released a statement following a disappointing fifth-place finish, stating: "Change is necessary in order for the club to keep moving forward."

The Reds decided to appoint Andoni Iraola following his wave of success with Bournemouth, having guided the Cherries to their first-ever European finish last year.

He took his old side on an 18-match unbeaten run to finish in sixth spot, with the Spaniard employing a fast-paced style that heavily relies on athletic players to press and transition.

Similarly to Maresca at City, Iraola joins the Merseyside club at a time of change, with legends like Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson having left in the summer.

10 The Chelsea role will be Alonso's third as a manager Credit: Getty

Chelsea - Xabi Alonso replaces Liam Rosenior

Xabi Alonso was chosen by Chelsea as the permanent successor to Liam Rosenior, who was sacked in April only three months after he took over from Maresca.

Liverpool legend Alonso is no stranger to English football but he is now set to begin his Premier League managerial career this season with the Blues.

He made his first-team managerial debut in the dugout at Bayer Leverkusen, where he won the club their first-ever Bundesliga title in his first full term in charge without losing a single league game.

A year later, he landed the Real Madrid job, yet failed to replicate his success in La Liga.

Alonso's tenure lasted only eight months before he stepped down following a difficult run of results, prior to being announced as Chelsea boss for the 2026/27 season.

The 44-year-old saw most of his success come with a back-three formation, and he is expected to revert to that system at Stamford Bridge.

Since arriving at the club, he sanctioned a British-record move for Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for £117million to signal his high ambitions for the upcoming campaign.

10 German coach Matthias Jaissle is set for Newcastle Credit: AFP

Newcastle - Matthias Jaissle replaces Eddie Howe

Matthias Jaissle has been backed as the replacement for Eddie Howe at Newcastle following his shock exit.

Former Bournemouth manager Howe came under pressure after a poor season, seeing Newcastle finish 12th in the Premier League.

Jaissle is a two-time Asian Champions League winner with Al Ahli - a club owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, like Newcastle.

Since the 38-year-old arrived in Saudi Arabia, his team has played 138 matches, winning 92, drawing 21, and losing 25.

His tactics have been heavily influenced by the Red Bull coaching model, with his sides built around aggressive high pressing and intense counter-attack.

His coaching style could be ideally suited to Newcastle, who have built a squad around intensity and athleticism.

10 It will be Rose's first managerial job in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Bournemouth - Marco Rose replaces Andoni Iraola

Marco Rose will be Bournemouth's new head coach next season after Iraola confirmed at the end of the campaign that he was leaving the south coast.

The German spent the majority of his playing career at Mainz 05 under Jurgen Klopp.

He also made his managerial breakthrough at the club as he took over their second team as player/assistant coach in 2010.

Three years later, he became Under-16s head coach at RB Salzburg in Austria before being named head coach of the first team in 2017.

Rose won back-to-back league titles and did not lose a home match during his two-year tenure.

He returned to Germany and oversaw Borussia Monchengladbach and Borussia Dortmund, securing Champions League at both clubs.

He eventually joined RB Leipzig and won the DFB-Pokal in 2023.

10 Arbeloa will be looking to guide Fulham to a top half finish for the first time since 2023 Credit: Getty

Fulham - Alvaro Arbeloa replaces Marco Silva

Nine years after he last played in the Premier League, Alvaro Arbeloa will return as Fulham’s head coach.

After spending five years at the club, Marco Silva decided not to renew his contract at the London-based club, opting instead for a new challenge at Benfica.

As a player, Arbeloa helped Liverpool reach the Champions League final before winning La Liga, two Copa del Rey trophies and becoming a European champion with Real Madrid.

After retiring, he took charge of Real Madrid’s Under-19s, then their B team, before becoming interim head coach of the seniors in January 2026.

They reached the Champions League quarter-finals and finished second in LaLiga, but he stepped down at the end of the season before signing his contract at Craven Cottage.

10 Pierre Sage is looking to make his mark at Conference League winners Crystal Palace Credit: Getty

Crystal Palace - Pierre Sage replaces Oliver Glasner

Pierre Sage faces the difficult task of replacing one of Crystal Palace's greatest-ever managers in Oliver Glasner.

Sage did not play professional football.

He got his break at Lyon when he was named interim manager of the first team and guided them to Europa League qualification, earning him the job on a permanent basis.

After leaving the club in January 2025, he was appointed at RC Lens that summer.

He led the club to their first Coupe de France trophy and secured qualification for the Champions League.

The 47-year-old's success caught the Eagles' attention following the open vacancy at Selhurst Park.

10 Glasner has revealed Forest had accepted Elliott Anderson would leave the club when he was appointed Credit: Getty

Nottingham Forest - Oliver Glasner replaces Vitor Pereira

Forest suddenly announced the departure of Vitor Pereira - despite the club previously intending to extend his contract earlier this summer.

Glasner achieved major success at Palace, delivering trophies in back-to-back seasons.

He secured the south London club their first-ever major trophy by winning the FA Cup in 2025, followed by the Conference League.

However, after his contract expired, he decided not to sign an extension in order to pursue a new challenge.

Though Glasner insisted his decision was made prior to the transfer window, he grew visibly frustrated with the club's hierarchy over squad management.

He publicly expressed feeling abandoned following the high-profile January sales of club captain Marc Guehi to Manchester City and Eberechi Eze to Arsenal.

Meanwhile, Glasner already seems to be backed financially at Forest following the arrival of talented midfielder Xaver Schlager, whom Glasner previously worked with earlier in his career.

10 O'Neil has faced two relegation battles - and survived both Credit: Getty

Ipswich Town - Gary O'Neil replaces Kieran McKenna

Kieran McKenna resigned as Ipswich manager just weeks after clinching a return to the top-flight.

McKenna cited his reasons for the surprise departure as his desire to take a break from the game and spend more time with his family.

Gary O'Neil, who spent two years played for Ipswich's big rivals Norwich City, has taken charge.

The 43-year-old was at Strasbourg for the second half of last season, winning 13 of his 27 games at the helm of the French side.

Ipswich were promoted as Championship runners-up last term and face a tough task to avoid heading straight back down again.

Sports.title: Jamie O’Hara threatens to ‘take Jason Cundy’s head off’ in explosive row over Tottenham
Sports.content:
Jamie O'Hara reacted furiously to Jason Cundy's suggestion he should be happy with Tottenham finishing 10th this season.

Former Spurs midfielder O'Hara has repeatedly insisted his old club 'are back' amid their substantial summer business – but, not for the first time, Cundy was having none of it.



1 Roberto De Zerbi heads into his first full season as Spurs boss with a raft of new signings at his disposal Credit: Getty

O'Hara and Cundy lock horns

The ex-Chelsea defender, who also played for Spurs, told O'Hara he ought to temper his expectations following Tottenham's back-to-back 17th-placed finishes in the Premier League.

O'Hara, however, was similarly derisory about Cundy's claim Chelsea will win the title.

Joining Cundy on a heated edition of The Sports Bar, O'Hara challenged his co-host, saying: "I think it's a bit rich you coming here trying to dig out Spurs fans for being hopeful and realistic about where we believe we can finish with them two top players [talkSPORT understands Tottenham are working on a double deal for Manchester City duo Savinho and Omar Marmoush] when you literally come on here, your first show back, and said that Chelsea are going to win the league."



Cundy retorted: "Yeah, because we've won it [before]."

A fuming O'Hara interjected: "I'm not saying we're going to win the Premier League. I'm saying we can finish in the top four. We've finished in the top four multiple times, so I'm not saying something we ain't done."

But Cundy told him he should be happy with a mid-table finish, urging: "Jay, Jay, 10th. Take 10th."



O'Hara continued in furious fashion: "Don't sit here and say, 'Oh well, we've won the Premier League'. We've finished in the top four before. We can do that again."

Cundy was not backing down, though, insisting: "Jay, if I give you 10th now, you're taking it. You're taking my arm off."



"I'm not taking your arm off for 10th," O'Hara replied dismissively.

"Both arms," Cundy offered in response – which tipped O'Hara over the edge.

'I'll take your head off'

"I'll take your head off if you carry on talking crap," he raged "No, no, seriously, don't annoy me."

Eventually, after admitting he 'really wanted to swear' at Cundy, O'Hara had had enough and walked out of the studio – much to his colleague's derision.

New-look Tottenham

Spurs have made six senior signings so far this summer, bringing in the likes of Sandro Tonali and Andy Robertson.



However, former Watford striker Troy Deeney told talkSPORT Tottenham have actually made their squad weaker.

In any case, there is just over a week-and-a-half to go in the transfer window, which shuts for Premier League clubs at 11pm BST on Tuesday, September 1.

Spurs and Blues about to get going again

The new Premier League season gets underway on Friday night, with Tottenham and Chelsea both in action in the following days.

And both sides begin the campaign with London derbies: Spurs travel to Brentford on Saturday evening and the Blues, in their first competitive game under new manager Xabi Alonso, are away to local rivals Fulham on Monday night.

Sports.title: Arsenal can smash all-time English football record in the Premier League this season
Sports.content:
Arsenal can smash all-time English football record in the Premier League this season

Arsenal have 'no competition' in the Premier League title race this season - they're going to break an all-time record.

That's the opinion of talkSPORT's Adrian Durham, who thinks the Gunners could win the league by over 20 points.



3 Arsenal have been tipped to go back-to-back and break records this season Credit: Getty

Mikel Arteta's side ended their 22-year wait for glory in the top flight last season, finally getting their hands on the trophy.

They finished above Manchester City by seven points to win the title, but Durham thinks that margin is going to grow.

Arsenal have spent more than £150million this summer, with another £50m set to be splashed on Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa.



£75m Bruno Guimaraes is going to be alongside Declan Rice in midfield, while Christos Tzolis already looks to be a star.

The fresh additions, on top of their already star-studded squad - while the rest of the 'Big Six' are all starting new eras - see them being tipped to do something very special this campaign...



Durham: Arsenal can win title by 20+ points

"It feels like it's going to be so, so easy," Durham predicted on talkSPORT Breakfast.

"In fact, on Monday night's kick-off show, I said that I believed Arsenal would break the record for the points gap at the top of the table at the end of the season.



"They won't just win the title, they'll win it by miles. I think it could be a 20-plus points margin."

He added: "There literally is no competition for Arsenal.

"They were so good last season and they've strengthened this season. I can only see one winner."

3 Durham thinks Arsenal have no competitors for the title this season Credit: Getty

Could Arsenal break the all-time record?

If Durham is right and Arsenal do go on to win the Premier League title by 20 points or more, they would make history.



No team has ever won the title by that many points, with Man City currently holding the record margin with 19 points.

City stormed to glory in 2017/18 under Pep Guardiola, winning 32 out of their 38 games and reaching 100 points in total.

They had won the league by April, going on to finish above rivals Manchester United by a record-breaking distance.

Man United are also on the list of biggest-ever winning margins, sitting level with Liverpool, who won the Premier League in 2019/20 by 18 points, just one short of equalling history.



Alex Ferguson's Red Devils won the league by 18 points in 2000.

3 Man City currently hold the record for winning the title by 19 points in 2018 Credit: Getty

Biggest title-winning margins ever in English top flight Manchester City - 19 points (2017/18) Liverpool - 18 points (2019/20) Manchester United - 18 points (1999/2000) Everton - 13 points (1984/85) Chelsea - 12 points (2004/05) Manchester City - 12 points (2020/21) Arsenal - 11 points (2003/04) Manchester United - 11 points (2012/13) Preston North End - 11 points (1888/89) Aston Villa - 11 points (1896/97) Sunderland - 11 points (1892/93) West Brom - 11 points (1919/20)

Everton are on the list too, winning the First Division by 13 points in 1984/85 to claim their eighth title at the time.

Meanwhile, Chelsea, Aston Villa, Sunderland, West Brom and Preston all feature in the all-time record books for their titles.

The Blues were led to the Premier League trophy by Jose Mourinho in 2004/05, with them coming out on top by 12 points.



Arsenal are already on the list of biggest margins as they were 11 points clear when they tasted success in 2003/04.

Could they end up breaking their own club record this year?

Or will Durham be right and the Gunners go on to stick their name at the top of the all-time history books above Man City?

Sports.title: Nick Kyrgios brutally mocked by Simona Halep following tennis star's positive cocaine test - after Australian ruthlessly berated former world No 1 during her doping ban
Sports.content:
Former World No1 tennis star Simona Halep has hit out at Nick Kyrgios following the Australian's positive cocaine test bombshell.

Kyrgios, 31, revealed he has been provisionally suspended from the sport after he submitted a sample while playing in Mallorca on June 22 that contained benzoylecgonine, a substance found in the class A drug.

Kyrgios said he took 'full responsibility' for his mistake and was 'deeply disappointed' in himself.

The Australian has been suspended since August 4, meaning he cannot play in, coach at, or attend any professional men's or women's tournament, including Grand Slams such as Wimbledon.

Kyrgios has staunchly opposed drug use in tennis and has regularly taken aim at stars who have tested positive.

He ruthlessly berated Halep while she served a ban for a doping violation in 2023, labelling her a 'potato'.

Simona Halep has hit back at Nick Kyrgios following his positive cocaine test

Australian tennis star Kyrgios publicly berated the former No 1 during her doping ban

Halep took to social media on Wednesday and said: 'Never kick someone when they're down'

'I'd imagine if I was taking similar things to be banned for 4 years, I'd have about 5 slams. Potato,' he wrote.

'I run on bananas and coke cola in 5 set battles. And my record in them speaks for itself. Maybe players should just stop taking shady s***.

'Look yourself in the mirror at the end of the day and say yep I did it right. Not hard.'

Following Kyrgios's admission of cocaine use on Wednesday, Halep took to Instagram to have her say, sharing a photo of a bottle of coke and a bunch of bananas in a not-so-subtle dig at the Australian.

She later posted: 'Never kick someone when they're down. Life has a strange way of changing positions and an even stranger way of revealing the difference between an accident and a choice.'

Kyrgios, 31, previously labelled Jannik Sinner and Iga Swiatek’s doping cases as ‘disgusting for our sport’. He said on Instagram at the time: ‘I only play with clean players’ – an indirect attack on Sinner after a fan urged him to play doubles with the Italian.

In February 2025, when it was announced the world No1 would serve a three‑month ban for his two positive drug tests, Kyrgios was first to take aim. The tennis player turned keyboard warrior posted a string of furious tweets.

He wrote: ‘So WADA come out and say it would be a 1–2 year ban. Obviously Sinner’s team have done everything in their power to just go ahead and take a 3‑month ban, no titles lost, no prize money lost. Guilty or not? Sad day for tennis. Fairness in tennis does not exist.”

Two days later, he continued: ‘And so you were innocent and we were getting fed that you were innocent but now you are suspended from playing the sport? Make it make sense. I’ve got multiple players in my DMs on how putrid this is, even Grand Slam champions. Cooked.’

Kyrgios said on social media on Wednesday: 'I wanted you to hear it from me first. I recently failed a drug test in Mallorca after testing positive for cocaine.

'I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it.

'I am sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors, and everyone close to me. Above all, I'm sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I'm deeply disappointed in myself.

'I'm not going to make excuses, but I do want to give some context about where I've been. The last couple of years of injuries have taken a huge toll on me, both physically and mentally.

'My body hasn't been able to do what my mind expects it to do, and coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined.

'I've always said I didn't choose tennis - tennis chose me. But letting go of something that has been my whole life is one of the hardest things I've ever had to face. At times I've felt helpless and alone.

Kyrgios admitted to testing positive for cocaine while he was in Majorca, Spain

'None of that excuses what I did.

'However, the good news is that this has given me a wake-up call. For the next 28 days, I'll be stepping away from social media and public life while I focus on getting myself right.

'I'd ask that people respect my privacy during that time, and most importantly the privacy of my family.

'I'm sorry. I'll do the work and come back better. Nick.'

Kyrgios played in Majorca at the Association of Tennis Professionals 250 event in late June, losing his singles match to fellow Australian Adam Walton in straight sets on June 22.

He later withdrew from the doubles, where he and partner John-Patrick Smith had been due to play Austin Krajicek and Nikola Mektic the following day.

The International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA), the sport's anti-doping body, has since announced that Kyrgios has been handed a mandatory provisional suspension.

A statement read: 'The International Tennis Integrity Agency has provisionally suspended Australian tennis player Nick Kyrgios under the Tennis Anti-Doping Programme.

'Kyrgios provided a sample during an ATP 250 event in Mallorca, Spain, on June 22, 2026. On July 17, 2026, a World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)-accredited laboratory confirmed the presence of benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

'Cocaine is a stimulant and substance of abuse on the WADA Prohibited List and is banned in competition under the Tennis Anti-Doping Programme. If taken out of competition, reduced sanctions apply for substances of abuse.

'Because of the nature of the substance, a provisional suspension is mandatory and has been in place since August 4, 2026.

'Kyrgios, who reached a career-high world singles ranking of 13 in October 2016, has the right to appeal the provisional suspension, but has not done so to date.

'As with all Tennis Anti-Doping Programme cases, ITIA support is available to Kyrgios.

'While suspended, Kyrgios is not allowed to play in, coach at, or attend any events organised or sanctioned by World Tennis, WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams, or any national association.'

Sports.title: TNT Sport bosses left bemused by Joe Cole after pundit bizarrely claimed Hull City have arrived in the Premier League 'through the back door' and he snubbed call to cover opening game vs Man United
Sports.content:
TNT Sport bosses left bemused by Joe Cole after pundit bizarrely claimed Hull City have arrived in the Premier League 'through the back door' and he snubbed call to cover opening game vs Man United

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Joe Cole has sparked a furious response from Hull City fans after claiming the Tigers are already relegated - and saying he put his phone on ‘do not disturb’ to ensure he would not have to be a pundit for TNT Sports at their season opener against Manchester United tomorrow night.

The former Chelsea and England man has triggered outrage in East Yorkshire thanks to comments he made with former West Ham team-mate Carlton Cole on a podcast.

When asked who would be going down this season, Cole said ‘Hull are gone, man’ before claiming that they had arrived in the Premier League ‘through the back door’.

He then added that he had ‘a confession to make’, saying he had been contacted by TNT Sports who ‘tried to slip in Hull on the first day of the season’. ‘I put my phone on Do Not Disturb,’ he said.

Hull City are GOING DOWN! 🗣️🐯



The lads don’t rate Hull’s chances this season 🥺



Watch in full 👉 https://t.co/PuonqV3D90#TheDressingRoom #PremierLeague #PL pic.twitter.com/B1xa8RV4nI — The Dressing Room Podcast (@dressingroomaa) August 19, 2026

Joe Cole has risked the wrath of Hull City fans with comments made on his podcast

Daily Mail Sport understands the comments have left bosses at TNT Sports bemused, with insiders saying Cole was not down to cover the opener at the MKM Stadium, and never had been.

Regardless, it has stoked plenty of emotion in Hull. Sources have disclosed that players and staff are well aware of what was said and intend to use it as motivation for what would appear to be a tough mission ahead.

Fans have taken to social media to highlight what they see as a ‘condescending’ and ‘disrespectful’ attitude, with some even claiming the newly-promoted club, who won the Championship play-off final, should ban Cole from its stadium.

Sports.title: Inside story of Tottenham's summer: A new mood behind the scenes, how Roberto De Zerbi got his wish and Conor Gallagher's changed role, what Pedro Porro's welcome reveals, a new 'grown-up' transfer strategy and the deals still to be done
Sports.content:
Early summer optimism has faded into familiar murmurings of apprehension among some Tottenham fans as the new season looms and another transfer deadline appears on the horizon.

Spurs remain short of reinforcements in the forward department but there is a quiet confidence inside the club that they can deliver up to three new strikers to satisfy Roberto De Zerbi and have a season free of the angst of the past two.

Daily Mail Sport brings you the story of Tottenham's summer and the latest from the Spurs camp ahead of their season-opening clash at Brentford on Saturday tea-time.

Roberto De Zerbi has had plenty of time on the training ground to build on the positive start he made at Tottenham last season

On the front line

Omar Marmoush and Savinho have been clear and solid targets for some time and talks appear to be advancing with Manchester City for the attacking pair.

Cody Gakpo is another, seen primarily by Spurs as a wide player rather than a centre forward, although any move for him is unlikely to develop until Liverpool have made signings of their own.

None are prolific goalscorers, although Marmoush was operating at a rate close to a goal a game for Eintracht Frankfurt in the Bundesliga season when City signed him in January 2025. In the Premier League, the Egyptian has 10 in 37 appearances. Savinho only two in 53. Gakpo, 32 in 127.

But they would all come from the top of the table. Gakpo, 27, was a champion in 2025. Savinho, 22, has spent two years at an elite environment at City, and has scope to improve. It's a similar story with Marmoush, 27.

Adding that Premier League experience, winning mentality and leadership has been a central theme of the Spurs recruitment drive. If they can deliver these three that will be nine signings, all of whom were playing in the Premier League last season and all senior internationals. That would be a major summer overhaul unlike anything Spurs have attempted in a long time.

There is no interest at present in Nicolas Jackson or Folarin Balogun.

Spurs are trying to bring in Man City's Omar Mamoush to give them more goal threat

Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo is another player Tottenham are interested in

De Zerbi's summer vibes

It is worth remembering the progress already made under De Zerbi before the transfer window even started. Eleven points from seven games and reviving players who looked spent under Thomas Frank and Igor Tudor.

None more so than Antonin Kinsky, who will start the season as No 1 goalkeeper. By the time they beat Everton to guarantee survival, Spurs were no longer performing like a relegation side.

Micky van de Ven who seemed disillusioned and looking for an exit six months ago saw enough he liked to refocus and sign a new deal, although he picked up an injury in pre-season and is a doubt for the opener at Brentford.

Amid the scenes of post-Everton relief, De Zerbi was spotted in conversation with Pedro Porro and owners Vivienne Lewis and Nick Beucher, stressing the need to extend the right back’s contract before the World Cup. It seemed like an inspired move when they did just that, because Porro was outstanding for Spain, returning as a world champion.

The guard of honour that marked his return included all the players, first-team staff, academy and training ground staff and was symbolic of the new unity valued and nurtured by De Zerbi.

World Cup winner Pedro Porro is given a hero's welcome by Tottenham fans during pre-season

Forging new bonds

The mood has been upbeat and positive according to insiders with De Zerbi given time and space to work as compensation for a pre-season tour on the other side of the world, in New Zealand and Australia.

Spurs rejected lucrative offers to play prestigious friendlies in Europe. Of the last three pre-season games, two were at the training ground and one at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, enabling De Zerbi to lock himself away for hours with his staff in preparation mode.

The Spurs boss has also reshuffled and strengthened his coaching team. Among the incomers are Andrew Crofts from Brighton and Agostino Tibaudi, who worked with him at various former clubs.

The first team have been based in The Lodge, the hotel accommodation at the training ground, while renovations have been taking place elsewhere on site, which has by chance helped generate closer bonds among the new group of players.

Twenty-five legends were invited to watch training last week and ate lunch with the players and coaching staff. De Zerbi hosted a table which included Glenn Hoddle, Steve Perryman and Gary Mabbutt. Archie Gray spent time with Pat Jennings listening to the former Spurs keeper recall clashes with his dad Frank and uncle Eddie, and Mikey Moore talked Rangers with Jermain Defoe.

The mood in training has been upbeat and positive according to insiders with De Zerbi given time and space to work

Gary Mabbutt (pictured meeting new signing Andy Robertson) was one of the Spurs legends invited to a lunch with the current team and playing staff last week

Foundation stones

Early recruitment forged the base of the team, which is the right way around. Andy Robertson, Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Martin Dubravka arrived and Kinsky, Porro, Van de Ven and Ben Davies signed new deals.

These together with Conor Gallagher, who signed in January, and Gray, who has captained the side in pre-season, can be expected to form the basis of the back seven or eight.

There is uncertainty around players such as Lucas Bergvall and Pape Matar Sarr, but this bedrock of the team has spent most of the summer working with De Zerbi. They have shaped up in pre-season with Gallagher operating as an industrious No 10 in a 4-2-3-1 shape. They look stronger and more aggressive at the back, albeit not watertight.

Conor Gallagher has been operating as an industrious No 10 in a 4-2-3-1 shape in pre-season

Buy high now, sell low later

The most radical change in the first summer window without Daniel Levy at the controls concerned the courage of their convictions. Spurs moved decisively for targets. They paid asking prices without hedging around too much pretending there were alternatives, despite leaving themselves more vulnerable to low-ball offers on those they wanted out.

There has been criticism. Some thought they could have held out for bigger fees on Cristian Romero (£34.2million) or Djed Spence (£30million) but the key was to move them on. Selling Spence on the back of a decent World Cup made sense. He was never anything but back-up for Spurs.

Interest would have faded and his value would have fallen had he started the season kicking his heels on the bench and De Zerbi would have had an unhappy player around his squad. And Romero had become a dissenting figure who had to go.

It’s true Spurs might have got more if they had played hard-ball over Guglielmo Vicario, who has joined Juventus on loan without an obligation to buy for £8.5million, but the Italian is a popular figure who has served them well.

Again, it is a more grown-up attitude from the club to enable a move to happen that suits all parties and not squeeze the deal for maximum profit.

Tottenham defender Cristian Romero had become a dissenting figure who had to go

Resisting a repeat of 2022

Antonio Conte was at the helm in the summer of 2022. Italian, like De Zerbi, his dream was to have all signings in for the start of pre-season so he could spend six weeks fine-tuning his strategy.

Just like this year, six came in early but they could not shift unwanted senior players. The market fizzled out, Conte grumbled and went into the season in a bad mood.

This year, the clear-out has been more efficient. Not only the established first-teamers – Tottenham have banked some big fees for youngsters and fringe players, with clauses galore for sell-on fees and buy-back options.

They could earn up to £20million on Will Lankshear and Ashley Phillips if they are successful at Middlesbrough and the add-ons come into play.

One they might live to regret is teenage centre-half Luka Vuskovic, who was sold to Brighton for £50million without playing a competitive game for Spurs after a successful season at Hamburg. Some good judges think Vuskovic is destined for the very top. It will be intriguing to see his progress in the Premier League this season.

Will Lankshear has made a bright start to life at Middlesbrough - he and Ashley Phillips could bank Spurs as much as £20million

Bee ready for Saturday?

Injuries niggle away and Dominic Solanke’s continued absence for much of pre-season after missing so much of last season with an ankle problem is a particular concern.

That plus the lack of signings up front leaves De Zerbi considering a front three for the opener against Brentford no stronger than the end of last season. Spence and Mathys Tel flanked Richarlison for the last game against Everton. As it stands, two of those look likely to start again, probably with Moore on the right.

Richarlison has three in six pre-season matches though, and by the deadline things could look different. Teenage winger Moore is primed for a loan move to Cologne if and when new forwards arrive.

James Maddison played 45 minutes in Sunday’s behind-closed-doors fixture against Hoffenheim. Fernandes played for 90 minutes and should be available. Mohammed Kudus is back training with the team, although Dejan Kulusevski will take longer on account of the delicacy of his longer absence.

Sports.title: Aston Villa table Ollie Watkins contract offer amid Saudi interest, Wrexham continue talks with ex-Man United star and Man City see Adam Wharton enquiry rebuffed: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... City see Wharton approach rebuffed Manchester City maintain an interest in Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton. The Selhurst Park club are reluctant to lose the 22-year-old this summer but have been making significant enquiries for midfielders in recent weeks. City are exploring a number of options including Manu Kone at Roma while they are advancing in talks to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille and are assessing the cost of a bid for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez. Wharton has been a significant Premier League performer in recent seasons and excelled in the Europa League Conference final but analysts at some top level would-be suitors have indicated his running statistics do not reflect someone who can fit into a high-pressing style. He continues to show on the pitch, however, an ability to find the right pass and shield his defence. Manchester City have seen an enquiry for Adam Wharton rebuffed by Crystal Palace Jones set for Inter medical Inter Milan expect Curtis Jones to arrive later today ahead of a £30.7million move from Liverpool. The Italian side have scheduled Jones' medical for midday on Friday. Inter bid £26.7m plus £4m in add-ons with a 10 per cent sell-on clause, offering a similar structure to the deal used to sign Djed Spence from Tottenham. Curtis Jones is set to sign a five-year deal with Inter Jones, 25, will sign a five-year deal with the Serie A champions. Meanwhile, Liverpool centre back Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, is in talks to join Levante on loan. Ndukwe does not qualify for a work permit in England so must be loaned out. Liverpool remain in talks over PSG winger Bradley Barcola. Sheffield Wednesday are to confirm the signing of Liverpool’s Northern Ireland international winger Kieran Morrison on a season-long loan. City identify Savinho replacement Manchester City have asked about Palmeiras winger Allan Elias as they consider replacements for Savinho. Allan is 22 but has not been capped by Brazil. Quick and skilful, he is not a goalscorer but has earned a reputation as a worker, willing to press. Newcastle United and Aston Villa have also scouted him in recent months. City are evaluating several options with Tottenham working on the deal to sign Savinho and forward Omar Marmoush. Villa table new contract offer to Watkins Aston Villa have made a new contract offer to striker Ollie Watkins. The 30-year-old is open to a move to Al Hilal who had a £38.5m offer rejected on Tuesday but are preparing a fourth offer for the England international. Watkins has scored consistently throughout his Villa career and his goals would be difficult to replace. Villa have maintained contacts over Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson who also has interest from Napoli but he is valued around £65m. Aston Villa have put forward a new contract offer to striker Ollie Watkins Wrexham make move for ex-United star Wrexham are continuing discussions with free agent Axel Tuanzebe. The 28-year-old Congo international left Burnley at the end of last season and has had interest from clubs but is interested in Wrexham's ambitious project. Wrexham are in talks to sign former Manchester United defender Axel Tuanzebe Hull advance in talks for Betis star Garcia Hull City owner Acun Ilicali has confirmed they are making progress on their bid to sign Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia and remain in talks for Deportivo La Coruna winger Yeremay Hernandez. ’I think probably, if nothing unknown happens, we will see him in a black and gold shirt. It has to be finalised, but I would say 90 percent of this deal is done. We are talking about the last details,’ said Ilicali. Pictures of Hernandez in Hull have been posted on social media, and Ilicali told BBC Humberside: 'We have to get the club side done and Yeremay also wants to come but it is a very vital, critical decision for himself. This deal is a very hard deal but we are somewhere where it looks positive. 'He is a young boy and it would change his life completely so he wanted to see where he would come. We will see in three, four days if this deal will be done or not. If it happens it will be a record for sure.' Race on for Black Cats Ta Bi West Ham and Burnley have expressed interest in Sunderland winger Jocelin Ta Bi. The 21-year-old only joined Sunderland from Maccabi Netanya in January and signed a four and a half year contract. He made one appearance in the FA Cup against Oxford United and then started against Fulham in the Premier League. As it stands, the Championship clubs have expressed interest but talks have not gone further.
